data.summary: Personal vs project constraints: user preferences recorded as constraints leak into every teammate's prime
data.detail: Colton (2026-09-15): users record personal preferences as constraints, and constraints are project-wide — prime's Active Constraints section shows every constraint to everyone regardless of who recorded it. Needs a personal/project split so a person's preferences apply only to them. Not built in v0.41.0 and no prior plan found in the graph. Per-person journal shards (v0.41.0) store who wrote each entry but the replayed graph is shared, so shards alone do not scope visibility. Open design questions: how scope is marked (field on constraint vs new node type), default for existing constraints, whether personal constraints are visible to teammates in search, how the recording agent decides scope.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Personal constraints rulings (Colton, 2026-09-15): constraints default to personal; teammates cannot find another person's personal constraints; agent judges scope by guidance and asks the human when unsure
data.detail: Personal preferences recorded as constraints were leaking into every teammate's prime and search. Ruling: a constraint defaults to personal (applies only to its recorder, by recorded_by email) unless it is true for anyone in the repo; the tool and skill carry guidance for judging, and the agent asks the human when unsure. Personal constraints are hidden from teammates across prime, search, node/neighbor lookups, dashboard and curation — not merely labeled. Rejected: labeled-but-visible (teammates' agents could still obey them) and a new preference node type. Known limit: hidden through the plugin, but still readable in the owner's committed journal file.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Personal constraints rulings round 2 (Colton, 2026-09-15): existing constraints stay project with no review prompt; only constraints can be personal; owner-only visibility, managers excluded
data.detail: Existing unscoped constraints stay project forever and owners reclassify by hand (rejected: owner review prompt, and bulk-converting to personal, which would hide real project rules like API limits). Personal scope applies to constraints only (rejected: patterns, which are usually shared conventions). Only the recorder can see or change a personal constraint (rejected: manager read access, which adds a roster-dependent leak path).
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Loss reporting leaked hidden node ids: journal_watch and rebuild loss checks computed from the raw graph, so a teammate's personal constraint id could surface in get_status.rehydrate_events and the session-start WARNING
data.detail: A viewer filter at storage read methods does not cover code that reads self._graph directly. Fix: the recorded known-ids snapshot and rebuild before-set hold only viewer-visible ids, while "missing" is computed against the FULL graph, so a hidden node still present is never falsely reported lost and a vanished teammate node is never named. Any future loss/diagnostic surface must use storage.visible_node_ids(), not graph.nodes.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: v0.42.0 built: personal vs project constraints — personal by default, hidden from teammates at one storage choke point
data.detail: Colton raised that users record preferences as constraints, which leaked to every teammate. Rulings: default personal with judging guidance and ask-when-unsure; teammates cannot find others' personal constraints; existing constraints stay project with no review; constraints only; owner-only. Built: cognition/scope.py (node_scope, visible_to by recorded_by email vs confirmed identity); storage viewer_email() (identity-file stat cache with racy window) and _visible/_visible_nodes applied to get_node, has_node, get_all_nodes, by-type, recent, uncurated, successors/predecessors, statistics, snapshot, find_nodes_by_ref, and write guards (update/remove node, add/remove edge); show_all_scopes constructor flag for remap_identity and backfill_identity CLIs. cognition_record gains scope (default personal for constraints, error on other types); cognition_update_node gains owner-only scope; search hits carry scope; prime splits Active Constraints (project) and Your Personal Constraints; dashboard personal chip; conflict-analyzer guidance; get_status doc notes visible-only counts. Sonnet review found a HIGH leak via loss reporting (fixed, discovery recorded), backfill missing show_all_scopes (fixed), missing abs() in racy check (fixed); accepted LOW: scope update writes whole metadata dict (no concurrent in-session constraint metadata writer today). Gates: full pytest 1687 passed + 2 pre-existing lifecycle failures (one backfill test double fixed after), svn suite 16 passed, ruff, render and parity checks.
data.author: Colton Dyck
